conflicts.fact: Rotation rule for 270° anticlockwise / 90° clockwise, and which rotations are listed as separate rules
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 gives the 270° anticlockwise rule as (x,y)→(y,−x) and then lists it as a separate fourth rule duplicating 90° clockwise. Lesson 4 lists only three rules. The two are consistent mathematically but Lesson 3's 'four rules' contains a duplicate; this is a minor presentation inconsistency.

conflicts.fact: Image of P(4,2) after 270° anticlockwise rotation vs. rule use
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 states the successive images of P(4,2) as (−2,4), (−4,−2), (2,−4), which is correct under the rules. No contradiction with Lesson 10, whose Q2 on −240° (equivalent to +120°) uses a rule not derived in any earlier lesson. Lessons 3–4 only cover multiples of 90°.

conflicts.fact: Direction of the turbine's spin and the positive-rotation convention
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the 'direction of spin (positive = anti-clockwise when viewed from the front)' is a fact about the turbine's rotation. Lesson 6 states every 120° anticlockwise turn maps the assembly onto itself. Lesson 10 says it holds clockwise or anticlockwise. The turbine's actual spin direction is asserted as anticlockwise in some lessons but is never established in the Lesson 1 video, where direction is not given.

conflicts.fact: Number of self-mappings in one full turn for the three-blade turbine
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 counts self-mappings at 120°, 240°, and 360° (three). Lesson 10 says the assembly maps onto itself 3 times in 360°, consistent. Lesson 6 also asks students to list all angles 'between 0° and 360°', which would exclude 360°, creating an inconsistency in whether 360° counts.

Lesson 1 and Lessons 8 and 10 give the driving question as 'Why do the blades ... always look the same no matter how far they rotate — and how can we use the mathematics of rotation to predict exactly where any point on the blade will land?' Lesson 5's teacher script reads the driving question as 'If we know one blade position and its rotated image, can we find the centre?'

conflicts.fact: Direction convention for the clock's minute hand within the sequence's positive/negative convention
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 states the minute hand sweeps 6° per minute and calls it a negative (clockwise) rotation, consistent with the convention elsewhere. However, Lesson 9 describes 'approximately 10 minutes per station' for four stations (40 min) plus presentations, while the teacher guidance spends 2–3 minutes per station. Timing is inconsistent.

conflicts.fact: Where the Ngong Hills turbine hub sits relative to the origin and blade geometry
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 models the rectangular 'base plate of the turbine hub' as ABCD with A(1,1), B(4,1), C(4,3), D(1,3), rotated about the origin which is the hub, so the hub's 'plate' does not contain the hub centre. Lesson 1 says the hub is the fixed centre point.
